doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

chapter: Learning to read, studio work and rock and roll feel
title: Sight reading and chordalizing in New York studio sessions
summary: He explains how he reads enough to get through sessions and why he got studio work: he loved pop and rock.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Did you ever do a thing that — this is something I have to do at the piano if I get it — I have to chordalize it. I have to look at what’s written and say oh well this is mostly a G chord here and etcetera.
Yeah. I’m going to start doing that. I don’t necessarily do that. I mean over the years and goodness gracious I became a studio musician in New York, you know and I learned how

to read enough, and to sight read enough to get through most dates, especially, certainly the treble clef, treble staff, and as much of the left hand as I could grab, and figuring out that there’s going to be a bass and two other bones — trombones on that. You know what? I don’t have to hit — you know some things like that. And I will still, I hate to admit it, but I will write in the ledger lines because that’s just what I have to do. A-C-E. But at the time it’s nice to see oh E and then bang I have it. And that’s the way I kind of learned I could get through sessions. But really they wanted, I think I got going in the studios ‘cause I really did love pop and rock & roll and I was not condescending to play it, I was dying to play it. The previous generation were kind of older guys didn’t really like it. Sure they could play it but there’s a difference than if you really love it.
